macro.title: US Defense Spending Surge After $22.9B Raytheon Award
macro.body: The Department of Defense's seven‑year contract with Raytheon for Tomahawk missile production injects a sizable, recurring fiscal stimulus into the US defense sector. Higher government outlays tend to support risk‑on sentiment and can lift equities tied to aerospace and defense, while also modestly boosting the US dollar as Treasury yields rise.
macro.bull: If the contract spurs broader defense‑industry earnings upgrades, US equities could rally, benefitting leveraged exposure.
macro.base: Markets absorb the news with limited upside, keeping equity momentum steady.
macro.bear: If the spending boost fuels inflation concerns, the Fed may tighten faster, pressuring growth stocks and leveraged ETFs.

macro.title: Escalating Iran‑Hormuz Threat Tightens Global Oil Supply
macro.body: Iran's warning of offensive actions in the Strait of Hormuz raises the risk of shipping disruptions for a key portion of world oil trade. Historical patterns show sharp spot‑price spikes when Hormuz tension peaks, which can reverberate through energy equities and commodity‑linked assets worldwide.
macro.bull: Higher oil prices lift energy stocks and commodity‑linked leveraged ETFs, adding upside to the portfolio's exposure.
macro.base: Oil markets may price in a risk premium without a sustained supply shock.
macro.bear: If the threat escalates to actual closures, a sharp sell‑off in risk assets could trigger volatility spikes, hurting leveraged positions.

macro.title: China Re‑starts July Oil Stockpiling, Signalling Demand Resilience
macro.body: Beijing's decision to replenish strategic oil reserves after a month‑long pause suggests a rebound in domestic demand and a willingness to support global oil markets. The move can buoy the Chinese yuan against the CAD as trade flows improve, while also tempering global oil price spikes.
macro.bull: A stronger CNY reduces CAD‑USD pressure, modestly improving the FX book and supporting Canadian exporters.
macro.base: FX impact remains muted; markets view the stockpiling as routine.
macro.bear: If the stockpiling triggers higher global oil prices, the CAD could weaken further, eroding FX gains.

news.headline: Nvidia finances OpenAI data center in Ohio – AI demand surge
news.body: Nvidia (NVDA) is providing financing for OpenAI's new Ohio data center, underscoring its central role in the AI infrastructure chain. This reinforces demand for Nvidia GPUs, supporting the massive unrealised gains in the portfolio's core NVDA holding.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Continued AI rollout accelerates Nvidia sales, driving the stock higher and lifting the portfolio's overall return.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: The news is priced in; Nvidia trades sideways, leaving the position flat.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Regulatory scrutiny on AI chips or supply‑chain constraints weigh on Nvidia, pulling the stock down.

news.headline: Raytheon secures $22.9B US defense contract – aerospace sector lift
news.body: The award to Raytheon (RTX) signals robust US defense spending, which can buoy aerospace and defense equities globally. While the portfolio does not hold RTX, the sector tailwinds may benefit related holdings such as BMO's aerospace exposure (BMO.TO) and broader market sentiment for risk assets.
news.exposure: BMO.TO ~$9,000 CAD (Canadian financial with aerospace exposure)

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Defense optimism lifts aerospace stocks, nudging BMO.TO higher.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Market digests the contract without major spillover; BMO.TO remains stable.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Higher defense spending fuels inflation fears, prompting a rate‑hike outlook that drags equities.

news.headline: China resumes oil stockpiling in July, first rise since Iran war
news.body: China's renewed oil stockpiling lifts global crude demand expectations, supporting oil prices. The portfolio's indirect exposure via energy‑linked equities (e.g., ENB.TO) could benefit from higher energy margins.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Oil prices climb 5‑7%, boosting Enbridge's dividend outlook and share price.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Markets view the stockpiling as a short‑term buffer; ENB.TO steadies.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: If stockpiling triggers a price spike that leads to demand softening, energy stocks could retreat.

daily_outlook: Today's mix of heightened geopolitical risk in the Middle East and fresh US defense spending creates a volatile backdrop; leveraged equity exposure could swing sharply, while energy and AI‑related holdings have upside catalysts.

risks.title: Volatility Regime Shift Risk
risks.context: 49% of portfolio (~$135K CAD) in 3x leveraged ETFs
risks.body: A rapid rise in VIX above 25 could trigger sharp drawdowns in FNGU, SPXL and UDOW, magnifying losses across the core of the portfolio.

risks.title: FX Drag Risk
risks.body: A sustained CAD appreciation of 1% would erode the CAD value of USD‑denominated holdings, reducing effective returns in the Investment and RRSP accounts.

risks.title: Sector Overlap Concentration Risk
risks.context: Tech stocks + leveraged tech ETFs represent ~70% of net assets
risks.body: Correlated moves in the semiconductor and AI space could amplify both upside and downside, limiting diversification benefits.

picks.thesis: U.S. defense spending is accelerating after the $22.9 bn Raytheon award; RTX stands to benefit from higher procurement cycles and offers a non‑tech, dividend‑paying exposure to offset leveraged tech risk.
picks.entry: Target entry $105–$110 CAD per share; consider adding $10K‑$15K CAD on pull‑backs.

picks.thesis: Canadian banks remain a defensive pillar with strong capital ratios; BNS provides exposure to the domestic financial sector and generates CAD‑denominated dividend income, useful for the upcoming home‑purchase cash flow.
Renewable infrastructure offers growth aligned with global decarbonisation trends and adds a low‑correlation asset to the portfolio, mitigating leveraged equity volatility.
picks.entry: Buy on dips near $38–$40 CAD; allocate $8K CAD.

strengths.text: Low cost basis with >1,700% unrealized gain; core AI exposure locked in.
High overall portfolio ROI (+83%) demonstrates effective growth orientation.
Tax‑sheltered accounts (TFSA, FHSA) have generated >120% returns, preserving capital gains.
Diversified across sectors: tech, financials, energy, and leveraged equity, providing multiple growth levers.
Liquidity in major U.S. equities and Canadian blue‑chips enables rapid rebalancing if needed.

concerns.text: Idle cash in the RRSP (~$20K CAD) is subject to cash‑drag, reducing overall portfolio efficiency.
Heavy reliance on 3x leveraged ETFs creates decay risk in sideways markets, especially as VIX hovers above 22.
FX exposure is concentrated in USD assets; a strong CAD would diminish CAD‑denominated returns.
Overlap between leveraged ETFs and individual tech holdings limits true diversification and may amplify sector‑specific shocks.
Upcoming non‑resident status (March 2027) will change tax treatment of future gains and may restrict contribution room.

strategy_short.text: Monitor VIX; if it breaches 25, consider trimming 3x leveraged positions by up to 20% to curb decay risk.
Deploy idle RRSP cash into the new picks (RTX, BNS) over the next 4‑6 weeks, focusing on pull‑backs.
Set up a CAD‑USD hedge using a short‑term forward contract to lock the current 1.3925 rate for the next 3 months.

strategy_mid.text: Rebalance sector exposure by gradually reducing leveraged tech ETFs to 35% of portfolio by Q2 2027, reallocating proceeds to renewable infrastructure (BEP.UN) and defensive financials.
Establish a systematic quarterly review of FX exposure and adjust hedge ratios as CAD moves, aiming to keep net FX impact under 5% of portfolio value.
Begin a $30K CAD contribution plan to the RRSP over the next 12 months to maximize future tax‑deferral before non‑resident status.

strategy_long.text: Position for a post‑pandemic AI infrastructure boom by maintaining a core NVDA exposure while adding selective semiconductor peers (e.g., ASML) once valuation gaps widen.
Build a diversified, low‑correlation income stream through Canadian dividend aristocrats and REITs to support the home‑purchase timeline beyond 2027.
Plan for eventual repatriation of overseas earnings in 2027 by pre‑positioning foreign tax credits and exploring a Section 85 rollover to a Canadian corporation if income levels justify.

tax.text: RRSP contributions remain fully deductible against Canadian taxable income; ensure the $30K planned contributions are made before the 2026 contribution deadline to capture the current marginal tax rate benefit.
Foreign dividend and capital gains from U.S. holdings will generate foreign tax credits; retain all 1099‑type statements to claim credits against Canadian tax liability.

Upon becoming a non‑resident in March 2027, future RRSP withdrawals will be subject to a 25% withholding tax unless a tax treaty applies; consider a partial Roth conversion before the status change to mitigate future tax drag.
